title: Feedback Design in the Shadow of Strategic Communication
abstract: arXiv:2611.13450v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study optimal feedback design when evaluations affect subsequent strategic communication within organizations. A firm designs public feedback about an employee's potential before the employee communicates private information about project-specific circumstances to a manager. While more informative feedback helps the manager make better decisions, it can also intensify preference conflicts and undermine the credibility of subsequent communication. We characterize the optimal feedback policy. First, full disclosure is either optimal for all prior beliefs or strictly suboptimal for all of them. In particular, it is optimal when preference conflicts are sufficiently small or sufficiently large. Second, when full disclosure is suboptimal, no disclosure is optimal for some priors, while partial disclosure is strictly optimal for some priors if and only if the number of messages in equilibrium communication varies with posterior beliefs. translated_title: 战略沟通阴影下的反馈设计
translated_abstract: 我们研究了当评估会影响组织内后续战略沟通时的最优反馈设计问题。一家公司在员工向经理传达关于项目具体情况的可信信息之前，会先设计关于员工潜力的公开反馈。虽然信息含量更高的反馈有助于经理做出更好的决策，但它也可能加剧偏好冲突并削弱后续沟通的可信度。我们刻画了最优反馈政策。第一，完全披露要么对所有先验信念都是最优的，要么对所有先验信念都是严格次优的；特别地，当偏好冲突足够小或足够大时，完全披露是最优的。第二，当完全披露为次优时，对某些先验信念而言不披露是最优的，而部分披露对某些先验信念严格最优，当且仅当均衡沟通中的消息数量随事后信念而变化。
tldr: 本文研究了当反馈评估会影响组织内后续战略沟通时的最优反馈设计，证明完全披露要么对所有先验信念都最优、要么对所有先验信念都严格次优，并刻画了部分披露严格最优的条件。
en_tdlr: This paper studies optimal feedback design when evaluations affect subsequent strategic communication within organizations, showing that full disclosure is either optimal for all prior beliefs or strictly suboptimal for all of them, and characterizing exactly when partial disclosure is strictly optimal.
